def: Including all or nearly all elements; complete.
ex: The report offers a comprehensive review of the research.

def: To consist of; to make up.
ex: The collection comprises over 2,000 letters.

def: Existing or happening at the same time.
ex: The two concurrent studies reached the same result.

def: To grant a title or benefit; to discuss.
ex: The university conferred an honorary degree on her.

def: To comply with rules or standards; to behave like others.
ex: Students felt pressure to conform.

def: Following as a result.
ex: The drought and consequent crop failures caused hardship.

def: Notably large in size or amount.
ex: The project required considerable patience.

def: To make up or form; to be equivalent to.
ex: This act constitutes a breach of the contract.

def: Living or occurring at the same time; modern.
use: Two meanings: of the same era, or current.
ex: Shakespeare's contemporaries admired his plays.

def: (v.) To hold a conversation; (n.) the opposite.
ex: Wealth doesn't guarantee happiness, and the converse is also true.

def: Extremely important; decisive.
ex: Bees play a crucial role in pollination.

def: To reach a conclusion by reasoning.
ex: From the tracks, she deduced that a deer had passed.

def: To discover or notice the presence of.
use: Used for signals, errors, and diseases.
ex: The instrument can detect tiny earthquakes.

def: To give time or resources to a cause.
ex: She devoted her life to studying whales.

def: To take the place of; to force from a usual place.
use: Used for people, species, and water.
ex: The flood displaced thousands of residents.

def: Recognizably different; clear.
ex: Each region has its own distinct dialect.

def: Special importance given to something.
ex: The school places great emphasis on reading.

def: To meet unexpectedly; to face a difficulty.
use: Used for people, problems, and animals.
ex: The explorers encountered fierce storms.

def: To improve the quality or value of.
use: Used for performance, flavor, and images.
ex: Spices enhance the flavor of the soup.

def: Very large.
ex: The project had an enormous impact on the city.

def: Equal in value, meaning, or effect.
ex: A mile is roughly equivalent to 1.6 kilometers.

def: To wear away gradually.
ex: Waves slowly eroded the cliffs.
Repeated delays eroded public trust.

def: Occurring at the end of a process.
ex: The eventual winner was a newcomer.

def: To develop gradually.
use: Used for species, ideas, and technologies.
ex: Her style evolved over decades.

def: To be greater than; to go beyond.
ex: Sales exceeded the company's forecast.

def: To deny access to; to leave out.
ex: The study excluded participants under 18.

def: To show or display; (n.) a public display.
ex: The patients exhibited similar symptoms.

def: To uncover; to make vulnerable; to reveal wrongdoing.
use: Exposed to sunlight; exposed a scandal.
ex: The reporter exposed corruption in the city council.

def: Belonging to or coming from outside.
ex: External pressures forced the company to change.

def: To rise and fall irregularly.
use: Used for prices, temperatures, and moods.
ex: Gas prices fluctuate with the seasons.

def: About to happen; willing to share information.
use: A forthcoming book; she was not forthcoming.
ex: The witness was not forthcoming about what she saw.

def: To produce or create.
use: Used for energy, ideas, and interest.
ex: Wind turbines generate electricity.

def: To promise with certainty.
ex: Hard work does not guarantee success.

def: As a consequence; for this reason.
ex: The roads were icy; hence the delay.

def: A proposed explanation that can be tested.
ex: The experiment supported the researchers' hypothesis.

def: Lacking knowledge or awareness.
use: 'Ignorant of' a fact; not necessarily an insult.
ex: Early sailors were ignorant of the continent's existence.

def: To show to be involved in a crime or cause.
ex: The study implicated poor diet in the illness.

def: To suggest without stating directly.
ex: Her silence seemed to imply disapproval.

def: To force something unwelcome on someone.
ex: The city imposed a curfew.

def: To include as part of a whole.
use: Used for ideas, materials, and suggestions.
ex: The architect incorporated local stone into the design.

def: Existing at the beginning.
ex: Initial reactions to the film were mixed.

def: To introduce new methods or ideas.
ex: Companies must innovate to survive.

def: A deep understanding of a person or thing.
ex: The diary offers insight into daily life during the war.

def: To combine into a whole; to bring into equal membership.
ex: The new system integrates data from many sensors.

def: Honesty and strong moral principles; wholeness.
ex: The judge was known for her integrity.

def: Belonging naturally; essential.
ex: The ring has little intrinsic value but great sentimental value.

def: To call on as support or authority; to bring to mind.
use: Invoke a law, a memory, or a principle.
ex: The lawyer invoked her client's right to remain silent.

def: To impose a tax or fine.
ex: The king decided to levy a tax on salt.

def: In the same way; also.
ex: The first study found no effect; likewise, the second.
src: New Academic Word List (Browne, Culligan & Phillips, CC BY-SA 4.0)

def: Fully developed; (v.) to become fully developed.
ex: The trees take ten years to mature.

def: To make partial changes to.
use: Used for plans, designs, and genes.
ex: The team modified the design after testing.

def: Shared by two or more parties.
ex: The partnership was based on mutual trust.

def: To cancel out the effect of; to deny.
ex: The cost of shipping negated any savings.

def: In spite of that.
ex: It was raining; nevertheless, the game went on.

def: An idea or belief.
ex: The study challenges the notion that older adults can't learn new skills.

def: In spite of.
use: Formal; can come before or after a noun.
ex: Notwithstanding the bad weather, the event was a success.

def: (adj.) Not influenced by personal feelings; (n.) a goal.
ex: Scientists try to remain objective.

def: To counterbalance or compensate for.
ex: Higher prices were offset by better quality.

def: Continuing; still in progress.
ex: The investigation is ongoing.

def: Side by side and equally distant; similar.
ex: The author draws a parallel between the two revolutions.

def: Accepting what happens without active response.
ex: Viewers are often passive consumers of advertising.

def: To become aware of through the senses; to understand in a particular way.
ex: Dogs perceive sounds humans cannot hear.

def: To continue firmly despite difficulty; to continue to exist.
ex: The myth persists despite evidence against it.

def: A particular way of viewing things; a point of view.
use: Common in questions about narrators and authors.
ex: The story is told from the perspective of a child.

def: To present a problem or question; to sit for a portrait.
use: Pose a threat, pose a question.
ex: Rising seas pose a threat to coastal cities.

def: Exact and accurate.
use: The SAT's own question asks for the 'most logical and precise' word.
ex: The recipe calls for precise measurements.

def: Most important; (n.) the head of a school.
ex: The principal cause of the decline was overfishing.

def: Existing or coming before.
ex: No prior experience is required.

def: To forbid by law or rule.
ex: The park prohibits camping near the lake.

def: The possibility of a future event; a view.
ex: The prospect of rain worried the farmers.

def: To follow or chase; to seek to achieve.
use: Pursue a goal, a career, or a suspect.
ex: She pursued a career in medicine.

def: Far-reaching or thorough; favoring extreme change.
ex: The invention brought radical changes to farming.

def: To remove impurities; to improve by small changes.
ex: Researchers refined their methods after the first trial.

def: Unwillingness or hesitation.
ex: Despite his reluctance, he agreed to speak.

def: (v.) To settle or find a solution; to decide firmly; (n.) determination.
use: Resolve a dispute; strengthen one's resolve.
ex: The two sides resolved their differences.

def: To move backward; to make the opposite of what it was.
use: Reverse a decision, reverse a trend.
ex: The new policy reversed years of decline.

def: Unable to bend; strict and unchangeable.
ex: The school's rigid schedule left little free time.

def: The extent of an area or subject that something deals with.
use: The scope of a study, beyond the scope.
ex: That question is beyond the scope of this report.

def: Only; single.
ex: Her sole aim was to help others.

def: To a moderate extent.
use: Softens a claim; SAT answers often hinge on such qualifiers.
ex: The results were somewhat surprising.

def: Lower in rank or importance.
ex: In the novel, personal desires are subordinate to duty.

def: Money granted by the government to help an industry or keep prices low.
ex: Farm subsidies keep food prices stable.

def: A person or thing acting in place of another.
ex: Honey can substitute for sugar in many recipes.

def: A person or thing that follows another.
ex: The king named his son as his successor.

def: To halt temporarily; to hang.
use: Suspend a game; suspended in water.
ex: Officials suspended the race because of lightning.

def: Lasting for only a limited time.
ex: The bridge closure is only temporary.

def: To bring to an end.
use: Formal; used for contracts and processes.
ex: The company terminated its contract with the supplier.

def: To cause an event or reaction.
ex: The earthquake triggered a tsunami.

def: To experience or be subjected to.
ex: Caterpillars undergo a dramatic transformation.

def: To be the basis or cause of.
ex: Poverty underlies many health problems.

def: To commit to and begin a task.
ex: The team will undertake a five-year study of the reef.

def: To break a rule or agreement; to disrespect.
ex: The company violated safety regulations.

def: Done by choice, not by force.
ex: Participation in the survey was voluntary.

def: In contrast to the fact that.
ex: Frogs have smooth skin, whereas toads have bumpy skin.

def: To make sure a law or rule is obeyed.
ex: Police enforced the new speed limit.

def: To recognize the value of; to understand fully; to rise in value.
use: Several meanings: appreciate help, appreciate a difficulty, property appreciates.
ex: Few people appreciated how risky the plan was.

def: To decrease; to refuse politely.
use: A decline in numbers; decline an invitation.
ex: Bee populations have declined sharply.
